item.content:encoded:
Fiction or not, it's kind of creepy when you open a "new to you" SCP, and the depicted object is sitting on a shelf next to you.

All in all, I really liked this one. Not the most original premise (not a critique, it's almost impossible to come up with something truely original), but very well executed. I especially liked the edge of danger that comes from interacting with the story and staying in too long. Could have turned into a boring holodeck ripoff SCP without that added flavor. +1

item.title: Density
item.content:encoded:
Scrapings from the surface of SCP revealed a composition of 99% Sn, 0.5% Cu, 0.3% Sb, and 0.2% Pb, consistent with high-grade pewter. However, it is unclear whether SCP-826 is solid pewter or whether the pewter is merely a plating for some unknown element

The problem with this is that the density of a pewter that's 99% tin, 0.5% copper, 0.3% antimony, and 0.2% lead, is known (or can be calculated to several significant figures). The volume and weight of the SCP can be measured directly, and the Foundation should have thought of this.

So there should be a note saying either that density measurements indicate that it is solid pewter, or that it isn't.
